correctness.rationale: A nonzero source is a rotation class of positive zero gaps, including periodic repetition and the single-one case. One counts 010 at each one, 101 at each unit gap, 001 and 100 once per longer gap, and 000 by remaining gap excess. This gives (R,t,r,0,t,r−t,0,0), including wrap-around below length three. A rotation of order d fixes precisely lists repeated d times with d dividing r,t,R; the reduced block need not be primitive (the word 'primitive' at RESULT.md line 30 is inapt, but the formula correctly counts all reduced blocks). The singleton distinctions follow from one long gap, one excess zero in equal-length gaps, or a unique short gap with no excess. For at least two long and two short gaps, one versus two cyclic runs of long gaps produces distinct profiles of gap types and thus distinct source necklaces in the same read fiber. For one short gap it anchors distinct excess locations; with no short gap and excess at least two, concentrating versus splitting the excess gives distinct sources. The series, first ambiguity at n=8, and growth constants follow. A new bitmask reproduction checked all oriented signatures and 147 observed fiber sizes over n=1..16, both series, and the ambiguity boundary; /workspace/branches/replay-cyclic.py. The related-work assertion about non-implication from four-gram work is independently false, as explained under originality.

evidence: For fixed (r,t,R), E=r−t, G=t−B, A=R−B. If R=0 the only refinement has B=A=0; if R>0 there is exactly one feasible finer profile for each B=1..min(t,R).

For R>0, in the prior divisor sum d must divide r,t,R,B. Factoring out binom(r/d,t/d), the remaining sum over b=B/d is sum_b binom(t/d,b) binom(R/d−1,b−1) = binom(R/d+t/d−1,t/d−1) by Vandermonde. For R=0 the second prior fiber formula is already the asserted one.

For R>=2 and t>=2 there are at least two feasible finer profiles. Otherwise a unique finer profile exists for nonalternating sources, and it is singleton exactly for t=1, or R=0 and min(t,r−t)<=1, or R=1 and r=t. These are exactly the frozen singleton cases. The projected feasibility inequalities and these cases give the two geometric-series counts and the first ambiguity at (n,r,t,R)=(8,2,2,2).
